identity.action: Z.ai releases GLM-5.4, its first Loop Transformer flagship, on hosted plans
identity.dateBasis: Dated 2026-11-23 per Z.ai official blog bundle metadata and independent Nov 23 coverage.
identity.deduplicationReason: Distinct new flagship model version (GLM-5.4) following earlier GLM-5.3 events.

classification.reason: Verified action is hosted product rollout (GLM Coding Plan/ZCode/Z.ai Chat); capability claims ('2T-3T comparable') lack published benchmarks or independent verification.

significance.rationale: L1 hosted model launch; architectural novelty is noteworthy, but benchmark proof, API access, open weights, and independent follow-on adoption are absent as of cutoff.
significance.whyNotHigher: Under L2-METHOD and L2-PRODUCT-ACCESS, independent_follow_on_works and unaffiliated_production_organizations are null, and even primary benchmark scores are unpublished.
significance.whyNotLower: Verified primary release of a 750B looped-transformer commercial model.

new_method_or_framework.rationale: Loop Transformer builds on Universal Transformer / recurrent-depth literature; Z.ai itself states 'The idea is not new' and provides no public GLM-5.4 benchmark evaluation yet.

independent_follow_on_works.rationale: Model weights are not yet released and no independent follow-on works exist within 3 days of launch.

consensus.reason: Hosted rollout is confirmed, while intelligence claims remain unbenchmarked and API/weights remain pending.

dispute.reason: Absence of published benchmarks is a documented evidence limitation rather than a factual contradiction of the launch.

evidence.quote: GLM-5.4 loops 28 layers of the GLM-5 base model for two iterations.
We plan to open-source the model weights responsibly after completing necessary safety hardening.
Z.ai, the Chinese AI developer also known as Zhipu, launched GLM-5.4 on Nov. 23, calling it its first flagship model built on a "Loop Transformer" architecture.
That is the company's claim: no benchmark scores for GLM-5.4 have been published, and a team member said they will come later [2].
